rulings.headline: Coach's Challenge: VGK @ CBJ - 6:14 of the First Period
rulings.result_text: No goal Columbus
rulings.explanation:
At 6:14 of the first period in the Golden Knights/Blue Jackets game, Vegas requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Columbus was off-side prior to their goal.  
  
 After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that Columbus' Cam Atkinson did not have possession and control of the puck when he entered the attacking zone,According to Rule 78.7, "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Toronto Video Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an "Off-side" infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Columbus Blue Jackets.  
  
 The clock is re-set to show 14:19 (5:41 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.  
  
 ---  
  
Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge  
 A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:  

1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.  
  
New for 2017-18: If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.  

2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or  
  
 A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.  
  
Updated for 2017-18:A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: MIN @ COL - 8:02 of the Second Period
raw.body:
At 8:02 of the second period in the Wild/Avalanche game, Minnesota requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Colorado was off-side prior to their goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Situation Room determined that **the Colorado's Mikko Rantanen tagged up prior to Nathan MacKinnon touching the puck in the attacking zone.**
**Therefore the original call stands - good goal Colorado Avalanche.**
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, **the Minnesota Wild are assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.** **Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**
A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18**: If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18**: A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

raw.headline: Situation Room Initiated Challenge: EDM @ LAK - 19:50 of the Third Period
raw.body:
At 19:50 of the third period in the Oilers/Kings game, the Situation Room initiated a review under the terms of a Coach's Challenge to review whether Los Angeles' Dustin Brown interfered with Edmonton goaltender Cam Talbot prior to his goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee determined that **Brown pushed Talbot's pad and the puck across the goal line.** According to Rule 78.5 (ix) "Apparent goals shall be disallowed by the Referee when a goaltender has been pushed into the net together with the puck after making a save."
**Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Los Angeles Kings.** **Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**
A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18**: If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18**: A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.headline: Video Review: TBL @ CGY - 4:43 of the Third Period
rulings.result_text: Call on ice stands, no goal Calgary
rulings.explanation:
At 4:43 of the third period in the Lightning/Flames game, the Situation Room initiated a video review because the puck entered the Tampa Bay net. The Referee informed the Situation Room that he blew his whistle to stop play before the puck crossed the goal line. The decision was made in accordance of Rule 31.2 which states, in part, that "the Referee may deem the play to be stopped slightly prior to the whistle actually being blown. The fact that the puck may come loose or cross the goal line prior to the sound of the whistle has no bearing if the Referee has ruled that the play had been stopped prior to this happening."

Additionally, Rule 78.5 states that apparent goals shall be disallowed "when the Referee deems the play has been stopped, even if he had not physically had the opportunity to stop play by blowing his whistle."This is not a reviewable play therefore the Referee's call on the ice stands - no goal Calgary.

rulings.result_text: Good goal Nashville
rulings.explanation:
At 9:33 of the first period in the Lightning/Predators game, the Situation Room initiated a video review to further examine a play that occurred at 9:11 (prior to Calle Jarnkrok's shot entering the Tampa Bay net at 9:33). Video review determined that Viktor Arvidsson's shot at 9:11 completely crossed the Tampa Bay goal line. According to Rule 38.6 "In the event that a video replay shows a goal was scored prior to the play being stopped, the Video Goal Judge will inform the Game Timekeeper and Official Scorer of the time and the amount of playing time left to be reset on the game clock and penalty time clocks (if applicable)."

Since Arvidsson's shot entered the Tampa Bay net prior to when Jarnkrok's did, Jarnkrok's goal at 9:33 is disallowed. According to Rule 78.6 "Only one goal can be awarded at any stoppage of play." Therefore the clock is reset to show 10:49 (9:11 elapsed time) and good goal Nashville.

raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: TBL @ DET - 19:00 of the Second Period
raw.body:
At 19:00 of the second period in the Lightning/Red Wings game, Detroit requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether a Tampa Bay player interfered with Detroit goaltender Petr Mrazek prior to Yanni Gourde's goal. After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee **confirmed no goaltender interference infractions occurred before the puck crossed the goal line.**
**Therefore the original call stands - good goal Tampa Bay Lightning.**
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, **the Detroit Red Wings forfeit their time-out.**
---
**Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**
A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18:** If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18:** A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.result_text: The original call is overturned - no goal Toronto Maple Leafs
rulings.explanation:
At 8:26 of the second period in the Canucks/Maple Leafs game, Vancouver requested a Coach's Challenge to determine whether Toronto was off-side prior to Morgan Rielly's goal.

After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that Toronto was off-side prior to the goal. raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: LAK @ VAN - 17:31 of the Second Period
raw.body:
At 17:31 of the second period in the Kings/Canucks game, Los Angeles requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Michael Chaput interfered with Jonathan Quick prior to Nikolay Goldobin's goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee confirmed no goaltender interference infractions occurred.
Therefore the original call stands - good goal Vancouver Canucks.
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, the Los Angeles Kings forfeit their time-out. **Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**
A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18**: If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18**: A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

**Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**

raw.headline: Situation Room Initiated Challenge: LAK @ NYI - 19:47 of the Third Period
raw.body:
At 19:47 of the third period in the Kings/Islanders game, the Situation Room initiated a review under the terms of a Coach's Challenge to review whether a Los Angeles player interfered with New York goaltender Thomas Greiss prior to Anze Kopitar's goal. After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee **confirmed no goaltender interference infractions occurred before the puck crossed the goal line**.
**Therefore the original call stands - good goal Los Angeles Kings.**
---
**NOTE:** In the final minute of play in the third period and at any point in Overtime (Regular Season and Playoffs), Hockey Operations will initiate the review of any scenario that would otherwise be subject to a Coach's Challenge.
---
**Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge** A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18:** If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18:**A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

raw.body:
At 15:56 of the first period in the Avalanche/Penguins game, Pittsburgh requested a Coach's Challenge to determine whether Colorado was off-side prior to Nathan MacKinnon's goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that **Colorado's Erik Johnson was off-side prior to the goal.** According to Rule 78.7, "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Toronto Video Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an "Off-side" infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed."
**Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Colorado Avalanche.**

A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.

raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: BOS @ SJS - 6:17 of the First Period
raw.body:
At 6:17 of the first period in the Bruins/Sharks game, San Jose requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether a Boston player interfered with San Jose goaltender Aaron Dell prior to Peter Cehlarik's goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee determined that the actions of **San Jose's Joakim Ryan caused Boston's Jake DeBrusk to contact Dell before the puck crossed the goal line.**The decision was made in accordance with Note 2 of Rule 78.7 (ii) which states, in part, that the goal should be allowed because "the attacking Player was pushed, shoved or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper."
**Therefore the original call stands - good goal Boston Bruins.**
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, **the San Jose Sharks forfeit their time-out.** **Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**
A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18**: If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18**: A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.result_text: Call overturned, no goal Los Angeles
rulings.explanation:
At 19:13 of the second period in the Lightning/Kings game, Tampa Bay requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Dustin Brown interfered with Lightning goaltender Peter Budaj prior to Anze Kopitar's goal.

After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee determined that Brown's actions caused Tampa's Braydon Coburn to contact Budaj before the puck crossed the goal line, preventing him from doing his job in the crease.The decision was made in accordance with Rule 78.7 which states in part: "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Referee ... determines that the goal should have been disallowed due to 'Interference on the Goalkeeper,' as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4."Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Los Angeles Kings.Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Tampa Bay Lightning retain their time-out.---Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge  
 A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.New for 2017-18: If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; orA play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.Updated for 2017-18:A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

raw.body:
At 2:28 of the third period in the Kings/Maple Leafs game, Toronto requested a Coach's Challenge to review the "Interference on the Goalkeeper" decision that resulted in a "no goal" call. After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee determined that **Toronto's Matt Martin interfered with Los Angeles goaltender Jonathan Quick before the puck crossed the goal line**.
**Therefore the original call stands - no goal Toronto Maple Leafs**.
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, **the Maple Leafs forfeit their time-out**.
---
**Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**
A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18:** If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18:** A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.headline: NHL issues statement on Coach's Challenge ruling from Thursday
rulings.result_text: League says offside review of Colorado goal against St. Louis was incorrect
rulings.explanation:
NEW YORK - The NHL issued the following statement on the Coach's Challenge in last night's St. Louis vs. Colorado game at 17:26 of the third period that resulted in an incorrect decision of no goal:

"St. Louis requested a Coach's Challenge to determine whether Sven Andrighetto of Colorado was off-side prior to the Avalanche goal. The video review decision determined the play was off-side but that determination was based on a play prior to the puck clearing the zone.Per Rule 78. 7 (Note 1) Coach's Challenge: 'Goals will only be reviewed for a potential "Off-Side" infraction if: a) the puck does not come out of the attacking zone again; or (b) all members of the attacking team do not clear the attacking zone again, between the time of the "Off-Side" play and the time the goal is scored.Although there was an off-side, it occurred prior to the puck clearing the zone which nullifies any goal review related to that off-side. The entry in to the zone immediately prior to the goal was on-side, therefore the goal should have counted."

raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: VAN @ OTT - 15:29 of the First Period
raw.body:
At 15:29 of the first period in the Canucks/Senators game, Ottawa requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Vancouver's Alexander Burmistrov interfered with goaltender Craig Anderson prior to Vancouver's goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee **confirmed no goaltender interference infractions occurred.** **Therefore the original call stands - good goal Vancouver Canucks.**
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, **the Ottawa Senators forfeit their time-out.**
---
**Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge**
A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18:** If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
**2. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18:** A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.headline: Coach's Challenge: MIN @ CHI - 10:32 of the Third Period
rulings.result_text: Good goal Minnesota; Chicago assessed minor penalty
rulings.explanation:
At 10:32 of the third period in the Wild/Blackhawks game, Chicago requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Minnesota was off-side prior to his Chris Stewart's goal.

After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that the actions of Chicago's Brent Seabrook caused the puck to enter the attacking zone and the call on the ice was upheld - good goal Minnesota Wild. raw.body:
At 10:32 of the third period in the Wild/Blackhawks game, Chicago requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Minnesota was off-side prior to his Chris Stewart's goal. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 83.1 which states, in part, that *"If a player legally carries or passes the puck back into his own defending zone while a player of the opposing team is in such defending zone, the off-side shall be ignored and play permitted to continue."*

After NHL Hockey Operations staff reviewed all available replays and consulted with the Linesman, the call on the ice was upheld - **good goal Toronto Maple Leafs**
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, **the New York Rangers are assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.**
---
**Rule 78.7: Coach's Challenge** A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
**1. "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-side" infraction by the attacking team.
**New for 2017-18:** If the result of the challenge is that the play was "On-side", the goal shall count and the team that issued the challenge shall be assessed a minor penalty for delaying the game.
2**. Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
**Updated for 2017-18:**A team may only request a Coach's Challenge for Interference on the Goalkeeper if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: PIT @ NSH - 18:25 of the Third Period
raw.body:
At 18:25 of the third period in the Penguins/Predators game, Nashville requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether a Pittsburgh player interfered with Nashville goaltender Pekka Rinne prior to Patric Hornqvist's goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee **confirmed no goaltender interference infractions occurred**. **Therefore the original call stands - good goal Pittsburgh Penguins.**
Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, **the Nashville Predators forfeit their time-out**.
---
**Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
b) **Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

**Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
b) **Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

Therefore the original call is upheld - good goal Boston Bruins.Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Panthers forfeit their time-out.---Coach's Challenge  
 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:a) "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.b) Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.3. After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee confirmed that **the position of Marchand did not by itself impact Berra's ability to play his position in the crease** and therefore no goaltender interference infractions occurred. **Therefore the original call is upheld - good goal Boston Bruins.**

---
**Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
b) **Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

Video review confirmed that puck crossed the Arizona goal line before the net became displaced. According to Rule 78.4 "The goal frame shall be considered in its proper position when at least a portion of the flexible peg(s) are still inside both the goal post and the hole in the ice. The flexible pegs could be bent, but as long as at least a portion of the flexible peg(s) are still in the hole in the ice and the goal post, the goal frame shall be deemed to be in its proper position. The goal frame could be raised somewhat on one post (or both), but as long as the flexible pegs are still in contact with the holes in the ice and the goal posts, the goal frame shall not be deemed to be displaced". Good goal Florida.

According to Rule 78.7, "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Linesman, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Toronto Video Room, determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an "Off-side" infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal New York Rangers.The clock is re-set to show 3:40 (16:20 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Washington Capitals retain their time-out.---Coach's Challenge  
 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:a) "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.b) Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.2. raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: WSH @ NYR - 16:45 of 1st Period
raw.body:
At 16:45 of the first period in the Capitals/Rangers game, Washington requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether New York was off-side prior to Mika Zibanejad's goal.
After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the linesmen, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that **New York's Ryan McDonagh was off-side** **prior to the goal**. According to Rule 78.7, "*The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Linesman, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Toronto Video Room, determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an "Off-side" infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.*" **Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal New York Rangers**.
The clock is re-set to show 3:40 (16:20 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.
Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, **the Washington Capitals retain their time-out**.
---
**Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
b) **Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.explanation:
At 10:19 of the third period in the Hurricanes/Stars game, Carolina requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Adam Cracknell interfered with goaltender Cam Ward before the puck entered the net.

After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee confirmed no goaltender interference infractions occurred before the puck crossed the goal line.Therefore the original call stands - good goal Dallas Stars.Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, the Carolina Hurricanes forfeit their time-out.---Coach's Challenge  
 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:a) "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.b) Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.4. **Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
b) **Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.headline: Coach's Challenge: FLA @ CGY - 12:12 of Third Period
rulings.result_text: Original call is overturned, no goal Calgary
rulings.explanation:
At 12:12 of the third period in the Panthers/Flames game, Florida requested a Coach's Challenge to determine whether Calgary was off-side prior to their goal.  
  
 After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the linesmen, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that Calgary's Lance Bouma was off-side prior to the goal. According to Rule 78.7, "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Toronto Video Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an "Off-side" infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Calgary Flames.  
  
 The clock is re-set to show 7:51 (12:09 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.  
  
 Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Florida Panthers retain their time-out.

rulings.basis: result line: Original call is overturned, no goal Calgary

rulings.headline: Video Review: NSH @ VAN - 15:10 of the First Period
rulings.result_text: This is not a reviewable play, therefore the final on-ice decision stands - no goal Nashville
rulings.explanation: At 15:10 of the first period in the Predators/Canucks game, the puck entered the Vancouver net and after the four on-ice officials huddled, the final on-ice decision was "no goal." The referee then informed the Situation Room that he was in the process of blowing his whistle to stop play when Ryan Miller covered the puck with his blocker, before the puck crossed the goal line. According to Rule 78.5, apparent goals shall be disallowed "when the Referee deems the play has been stopped, even if he had not physically had the opportunity to stop play by blowing his whistle." This is not a reviewable play, therefore the final on-ice decision stands - no goal Nashville.

rulings.headline: Coach's Challenge: PIT @ DET - 5:09 of Third Period
rulings.result_text: Original call is overturned, no goal Pittsburgh
rulings.explanation:
At 5:09 of the third period in the Penguins/Red Wings game, Detroit requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Evgeni Malkin interfered with goaltender Jared Coreau before the puck entered the net.After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee determined that Malkin's actions caused Detroit's Justin Abdelkader to contact Coreau before the puck crossed the goal line, preventing him from doing his job in the crease.The decision was made in accordance with Rule 78.7 which states in part: "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Referee ... determines that the goal should have been disallowed due to 'Interference on the Goalkeeper,' as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Pittsburgh Penguins.Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Detroit Red Wings retain their time-out.
rulings.description: Original call is overturned, no goal Pittsburgh
rulings.basis: result line: Original call is overturned, no goal Pittsburgh

rulings.result_text: Original call is overturned - no goal Flyers
rulings.explanation:
At 1:48 of the first period in the Flyers/Blue Jackets game, Columbus requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Michael Raffl interfered with goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky before the puck entered the net.The Referee determined that Raffl's actions in bumping the Columbus defender into the goaltender prevented Bobrovsky from doing his job in his crease. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 78.7 which states in part: "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Referee ... determines that the goal should have been disallowed due to 'Interference on the Goalkeeper,' as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Philadelphia Flyers.Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Columbus Blue Jackets retain their time-out.

raw.headline: Situation Room Challenge: DET@TOR 19:59 of 3rd
raw.body:
At 19:59 of the third period in the Red Wings/Maple Leafs game, the Situation Room initiated a review under the terms of a Coach's Challenge to examine whether a Detroit player interfered with Toronto goaltender Frederik Andersen before the puck entered the net. After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee **confirmed no goaltender interference infractions occurred before the puck crossed the goal line**.
**Therefore the original call stands - good goal Detroit Red Wings**.
---
**NOTE:** In the final minute of play in the third period and at any point in Overtime (Regular Season and Playoffs), Hockey Operations will initiate the review of any scenario that would otherwise be subject to a Coach's Challenge.
---
**Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
**b) Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

Therefore the original call stands - good goal Anaheim Ducks.Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, the Vancouver Canucks forfeit their time-out.---Coach's Challenge  
 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:a) "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.b) Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"  
 (i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or  
 (ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.2. **Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
b) **Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"** (i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or (ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

Therefore the original call stands - good goal Columbus Blue Jackets.  
  
 Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, the Winnipeg Jets forfeit their time-out.

At 14:18 of the second period in the Red Wings/Panthers game, Detroit requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Nick Bjugstad interfered with Detroit goaltender Jared Coreau before the puck crossed the goal line.The Referee determined that Bjugstad prevented Coreau from doing his job in his crease, in accordance with Rule 78.7 which states in part: "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Referee ... determines that the goal should have been disallowed due to 'Interference on the Goalkeeper,' as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4."

Rule 69.3 states that goals should be disallowed if "If an attacking player establishes a significant position within the goal crease, so as to obstruct the goalkeeper's vision and impair his ability to defend his goal, and a goal is scored, the goal will be disallowed."Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Florida Panthers.Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Detroit Red Wings retain their time-out.---Coach's Challenge  
 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:a) "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.b) Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: DET @ FLA - 14:18 of 2nd Period
raw.body:
At 14:18 of the second period in the Red Wings/Panthers game, Detroit requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Nick Bjugstad interfered with Detroit goaltender Jared Coreau before the puck crossed the goal line.
The Referee determined that **Bjugstad prevented Coreau from doing his job in his crease**, in accordance with Rule 78.7 which states in part: "*The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Referee ... determines that the goal should have been disallowed due to 'Interference on the Goalkeeper,' as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4.*" Rule 69.3 states that goals should be disallowed if "*If an attacking player establishes a significant position within the goal crease, so as to obstruct the goalkeeper's vision and impair his ability to defend his goal, and a goal is scored, the goal will be disallowed.*"
**Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Florida Panthers**.
Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, t**he Detroit Red Wings retain their time-out**.

a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.

(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

rulings.headline: Coach's Challenge: TB @ VAN - 1:55 of First Period
rulings.result_text: Original call is overturned, no goal Vancouver
rulings.explanation:
At 1:55 of the first period in the Lightning/Canucks game, Tampa Bay requested a Coach's Challenge to determine whether Vancouver was off-side prior to their goal.  
  
 After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the linesmen, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that Vancouver's Jayson Megna was off-side prior to the goal. According to Rule 78.7, "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Toronto Video Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Linesman, determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an "Off-side" infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Vancouver Canucks.  
  
 The clock is re-set to show 18:48 (1:12 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.  
  
 Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Tampa Bay Lightning retain their time-out.

rulings.basis: result line: Original call is overturned, no goal Vancouver

At 6:32 of the third period in the Red Wings/Islanders game, New York requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether a Detroit player interfered with New York goaltender Jaroslav Halak prior to Mike Green's goal.After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee determined that Detroit's Luke Glendening interfered with Halak before the puck crossed the goal line. According to Rule 78.7, "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Referee, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Toronto Video Room, determines that the goal should have been disallowed due to 'Interference on the Goalkeeper,' as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Detroit Red Wings.Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the New York Islanders retain their time-out.---Coach's Challenge  
 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:a) "Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal  
 A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.b) Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

**Coach's Challenge** 1. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge to review the following scenarios:
a) **"Off-Side" Play Leading to a Goal** A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the play should have been stopped by reason of an "Off-Side" infraction by the attacking team.
b) **Scoring Plays Involving Potential "Interference on the Goalkeeper"**
(i) A play that results in a "GOAL" call on the ice where the defending team asserts that the goal should have been disallowed due to "Interference on the Goalkeeper," as described in Rules 69.1, 69.3 and 69.4; or
(ii) A play that results in a "NO GOAL" call on the ice despite the puck having entered the net, where the on-ice Officials have determined that the attacking team was guilty of "Interference on the Goalkeeper" but where the attacking team asserts: (i) there was no actual contact of any kind initiated by an attacking Player with the goalkeeper; or (ii) the attacking Player was pushed, shoved, or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper; or (iii) the attacking Player's positioning within the goal crease did not impair the goalkeeper's ability to defend his goal and, in fact, had no discernible impact on the play.
2. A team may only request a Coach's Challenge if they have their time-out available and the Coach's Challenge must be effectively initiated prior to the resumption of play.
3. If the Coach's Challenge does not result in the original call on the ice being overturned, the team exercising such challenge will forfeit its time-out.
4. If the Coach's Challenge does result in the call on the ice being overturned, the team successfully exercising such challenge will retain its time-out.

raw.headline: Coach's Challenge: BUF @ OTT - 16:10 of Second Period
raw.body:

Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, **the Buffalo Sabres retain their time-out.**

rulings.result_text: Original call is overturned, no goal Winnipeg
rulings.explanation:
At 9:54 of the third period in the Jets/Wild game, Minnesota requested a Coach's Challenge to review whether Winnipeg was off-side prior to Toby Enstrom's goal.  
  
 After reviewing all available replays and consulting with the linesmen, NHL Hockey Operations staff determined that Winnipeg's Nikolaj Ehlers was off-side prior to the goal. According to Rule 78.7, "The standard for overturning the call in the event of a 'GOAL' call on the ice is that the Linesman, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the Toronto Video Room, determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an "Off-side" infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed."

Therefore the original call is overturned - no goal Winnipeg Jets.  
  
 The clock is re-set to show 10:14 (9:46 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.  
  
 Since the Coach's Challenge resulted in the original call being overturned, the Minnesota Wild retain their time-out.

 After reviewing all available replays and consulting with NHL Hockey Operations staff, the Referee confirmed that the actions of Carolina's Noah Hanifin caused Montreal's Daniel Carr to contact Ward before the puck crossed the goal line. The decision was made in accordance with Note 2 of Rule 78.7 (ii) which states, in part, that the goal on the ice should be allowed because "the attacking Player was pushed, shoved or fouled by a defending Player causing the attacking Player to come into contact with the goalkeeper."

Therefore the original call stands - good goal Montreal Canadiens.  
  
 Since the Coach's Challenge did not result in the original call being overturned, the Carolina Hurricanes forfeit their time-out.
